notes.jjo: Nyomwabazyo, yesterday. The day before is nyomwabazyo eriya.
notes.wiiki: Sande, a week, is also Sunday.
notes.ssaawa-emu: Ugandan time: hour one after sunrise is 7 o’clock.

guidebook.intro: Talk about today, tomorrow, the days of the week and the time. Ugandan time counts the hours from sunrise, so seven o’clock is “hour one”.

tips.title: Days are counted
body: The weekdays are numbered from Monday: **Orwokubanza** (the first), **Orwakabiri** (the second), up to **Orwamukaaga** (the sixth), Saturday. Sunday is **Sande**, which also means a week.
**Erizooba** is today (it also means the sun and a day); **nyenkya** is tomorrow, and **nyomwabazyo** is yesterday.

tips.title: Ugandan time
body: The day starts at sunrise, so 7 a.m. is **shaaha emwe** (hour one), 10 a.m. is **shaaha ina** and noon is **shaaha mukaaga**. To get there, take six hours from English time.
Ask **Ni shaaha zingahi?** (what time is it?). Half past is **n’ekicweka**: **shaaha ishatu n’ekicweka** is 9:30.

culture.title: Two rainy seasons
body: Western Uganda has two rains a year: the long rains, **itumba**, around March to May, and the short rains later in the year. Farm work and school terms follow them.
